newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower despite electronics rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower despite electronics rise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Saturday as good showings in the electronics and electrical gear sectors failed to lift the wider market, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 43.47 points or 0.67 percent lower at 6,431.95. Turnover was a relatively active T$44.26 billion.
Early buying of electronics pushed share prices higher at the open, but lingering selling from foreign institutions continued to dampen overall sentiment, brokers said.
Shares in the electronics sector gained 1.47 percent and those in electrical and machine equipment rose 0.59 percent to defy the wider selloff.
"Recent rises of high-tech shares overseas drew persistent buying interest in electronics, but the overall market sentiment is still bearish," said Tank Hung of Yuan Ta Securities.
Brokers said the market expected little from a morning central bank meeting that had not ended when trading closed.
"People are not crazy about the likelihood that the central bank will further ease its monetary policy after the board meeting," Hung said.
"Liquidity is already very, very loose. The problem is that people are not investing money in the stock market," Hung said. "There is very little the central bank can do at this moment."

Central bank vice governor Liang Cheng-chin said on October 11 that the meeting would have "nothing to do" with adjustment of monetary policy, echoing bank statements that the board would gather to review strategic policies.
The bank has said the board would review a proposal to set a direction to lower banks' reserve requirements and at the same time raise the liquidity ratio.
